subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing and actionable in these expense records.

judge.implied_focus: The nature/purpose of the asset or good being expensed (asset-centric characterization of expense records)

per_column.name: asset_category_primary
per_column.rationale: Directly types the asset being expensed (laptop, desktop, service), a core facet of the asset-purpose focus.

per_column.name: asset_portability_context
per_column.rationale: Characterizes the asset by portability/usage context, a coherent facet of the asset concept.

per_column.name: record_creation_signal
per_column.rationale: Provenance of how the record was created; a process/metadata facet only loosely tied to the asset focus.

per_column.name: vendor_brand_primary
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand of the asset is a strong attribute of what was purchased, supporting asset-centric analysis.

per_column.name: processing_lag_indicator
per_column.rationale: Timing/processing metric unrelated to the asset nature; belongs to a different (operational) focus.

per_column.name: asset_specification_richness
per_column.rationale: Describes how precisely the asset is specified, a facet about the asset/description quality.

per_column.name: asset_expense_purpose
per_column.rationale: The functional purpose of the expense (hardware provisioning, travel, service) is the central asset-purpose facet.

judge.rationale: Five of seven columns (category, portability, brand, specification richness, expense purpose) converge cleanly on a single, data-inferable focus: what asset/good the expense represents and why. This is coherent and not a grab-bag. Two columns (record_creation_signal, processing_lag_indicator) drift toward a separate operational/process theme, diluting the centering somewhat. Given the asset focus, the supporting columns form a genuine multi-facet structure (type, portability, vendor, purpose, specification granularity) rather than a single restatement or generic noise, and they enable real analysis such as spend by asset type, vendor concentration, and provisioning purpose. The focus is actionable — an analyst can investigate hardware vs. service spend, vendor consolidation, and portability/usage patterns. Scores are moderated by the two off-focus columns and by some near-overlap between asset_category_primary and asset_expense_purpose.
